name: Hindustan Unilever
line: India's largest FMCG company, the Indian arm of Unilever

fy26c.label: FY26 consolidated review (broker report via Business Standard)

brief.t: India's largest FMCG company, owned majority by Unilever, with brands like Dove, Lux, Surf Excel, Rin, Lipton and Knorr.
Led by CEO & MD Priya Nair since 1 August 2025; Nitin Paranjpe is Non-Executive Chairman.
Q2 FY27 (Jul–Sep 2026) revenue rose 14.5% to ₹18,226 crore, with 15% underlying sales growth, its best in 14 quarters.
Q2 FY27 net profit was ₹2,790 crore, up about 4%; costs rose faster than sales.
FY26 was the first year after the ice-cream business (Kwality Wall's) was demerged into a separate company.

timeline.t: Lever Brothers starts manufacturing in India; the company traces its roots here.
Merged GSK Consumer Healthcare India (Horlicks, Boost).
Priya Nair became CEO & MD, the first woman to lead HUL.
Ice-cream business demerged into a separate listed company.

model.how: HUL makes and sells everyday products in Home Care, Beauty & Wellbeing, Personal Care and Foods. It earns by selling huge volumes through millions of shops, keeping costs low through scale, and charging more for premium brands.
flow: Sells through distributors to lakhs of shops and online
Profit after costs, advertising and tax

glossary.FMCG: Fast-Moving Consumer Goods: everyday products like soap, tea, biscuits, sold quickly at low prices.
glossary.Revenue from operations: Money earned from selling products and services, before costs.
glossary.Net profit: What is left after all costs and taxes.
glossary.EBITDA margin: Operating profit before interest, tax and depreciation, as a % of sales. Shows how efficiently the core business runs.
glossary.Underlying sales growth: Sales growth after removing one-off effects (like acquisitions or tax changes). Shows real demand.
glossary.Underlying volume growth: Growth in the number of units sold, not just higher prices. The best sign of real consumer demand.
glossary.Distribution reach: How many shops and outlets stock the company's products.
glossary.General trade: Small neighbourhood kirana shops, the backbone of FMCG sales in India.
glossary.Modern trade: Supermarkets and organised retail chains like DMart or Reliance Smart.
glossary.Quick commerce: 10–30 minute delivery apps like Blinkit, Zepto and Swiggy Instamart.
glossary.Premiumisation: Consumers moving to higher-priced, better products, which raises profit per unit.
glossary.Brand equity: The value a brand adds because people know, trust and prefer it.
glossary.Demerger: Separating one business into a new, independent company.
glossary.Excise duty: A tax on making certain goods, such as cigarettes. It is collected by the company and paid to the government.
glossary.Segment: A separate business line reported on its own in the company's results.
glossary.Attrition: The % of employees who leave in a year.
glossary.Dividend: Part of the profit paid to shareholders, per share.
glossary.BRSR: Business Responsibility and Sustainability Report: an official yearly report on people, environment and governance that big listed companies must publish.

Finance.q: HUL's sales grew 15% but profit only 4%. Why?
Finance.a: Costs, especially raw materials and brand investment, rose faster, so the EBITDA margin fell from 24.0% to 22.6%.

Finance.q: Why does volume growth matter more than price growth?
Finance.a: Volume growth means more people are buying; price growth alone can hide falling demand.

Marketing.q: Pick one HUL brand and suggest how to grow it among young buyers.
Marketing.a: Choose a brand you know, define its target customer, and suggest one digital or quick-commerce idea with a clear message.

Marketing.q: How would you sell HUL products in rural Punjab?
Marketing.a: Small affordable packs, strong kirana distribution, local-language promotions and village fairs.

HR.q: How would you attract top talent to HUL's sales teams?
HR.a: Show fast growth paths, early responsibility through management trainee rotations, and strong training.

Sales.q: How would you increase sales in a town where our brand is weak?
Sales.a: Add outlets, improve shelf visibility, run trade schemes, and track sales by beat.

Operations.q: How would you reduce stock-outs across lakhs of shops?
Operations.a: Better demand forecasting, distributor stock tracking and faster replenishment.

Other.q: What do you know about HUL?
Other.a: India's largest FMCG company, led by CEO Priya Nair; Q2 FY27 revenue ₹18,226 cr with 15% growth.

I want to learn how great brands are built and sold at India's scale, from big cities to small towns like mine, and contribute to [your role] at the company that sets the standard in FMCG.
